subject: Post-call: LedgerCorp evaluation — integration blueprint & next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@ledgercorp.com>, Rajiv Patel <rpatel@ledgercorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed integration blueprint (action items)

Thanks again for the demo time today — great conversation. Below is a short post-call recap and a proposed blueprint for the PoC integration so we can align on owners and dates. Please confirm or flag anything I missed.

Summary of goals (as discussed)
- Primary goal: Validate generation accuracy & latency on LedgerCorp chat flows (customer support transcripts + ephemeral context)
- Secondary goal: Measure embedding-based semantic search for 30M docs ingest, and end-to-end cost per 1k messages

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Latency: median response time < 350ms for 512-token gen under expected concurrency (10 TPS)
2) Quality: >= 85% acceptance on your annotation set (50 eval prompts)
3) Embeddings: recall@10 >= 0.75 on the 5k sample queries
4) Stability: no more than 1% error rate over a 48h stress window
5) Cost: projected per-message inference cost within 20% of budget number you provided

Proposed PoC scope & milestones (6 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, review requirements workbook (attached), exchange non-prod credentials
- Week 1: SDK integration + API routing for request/response (sample code + test harness)
- Week 2-3: Data ingest & embeddings pipeline; streaming evaluation on chat flows
- Week 4: Quality evals & tuning (prompt sets, model variant selection)
- Week 5: Stability run & instrumentation (tracing, cost dashboard)
- Week 6: Acceptance & wrap (results deck + next-steps commercial discussion)

Ownership (suggested)
- Redwood: Karthik (technical lead) for SDK/API integration; Ben (commercial) for SOW and procurement follow-up
- LedgerCorp: Elena (product lead) and Rajiv (security/procurement)

Immediate asks for LedgerCorp (today)
- Confirm success criteria above or mark changes
- Share test account (non-prod) details and a service account for API keys
- Confirm whether streaming responses + tool-calling will be in scope (you indicated yes, but we need explicit confirmation)

Attachments: LedgerCorp_PoC_requirements.xlsx (workbook we used in call)

Next steps
- If you confirm, we will circulate a one-page SOW draft and schedule a 30-min kickoff next Tue or Wed.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@ledgercorp.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed integration blueprint (action items)

Thanks Priya — Matt and I reviewed this and the list looks right. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Success criteria: we accept the latency and quality targets but would like recall@10 >= 0.78 for embeddings if possible (our searches are high-precision).
- Streaming & tool-calling: yes, streaming is in scope; we will exercise tool-calling for a product lookup microservice (internal API). We need a short doc showing how Redwood handles tool calls and sig verification.
- Security: Rajiv will own the security questionnaire. He asked whether you can provide SOC2 scoping docs and data retention defaults for the PoC (retention in non-prod should be configurable).
- Timeline: kickoff next Wed (2028-11-15) at 10:00 PT works for us.

I'll share a short test dataset (5k records) and the service account details by Monday morning. Procurement will likely request a simple SOW + statement of work before issuing a PO — please send a draft.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Product Strategy | LedgerCorp
elena.morales@ledgercorp.com

Subject: Technical follow-up: SDK routes, streaming, and tool-calling details

Hi Elena / Priya — jumping in with more technical detail so your infra team can review before kickoff. High-level design and integration notes below.

1) SDK & API entry points - We will provide our Node and Python SDK examples. Primary endpoints for the PoC: /v1/generate (text gen), /v1/embeddings (vector), /v1/stream (chunked responses over SSE or gRPC streaming). - Auth: short-lived API keys for non-prod; we can also support mTLS for your CI runners.

2) Streaming behavior - Streaming will use chunked SSE by default; we can also enable gRPC streaming if you prefer binary frames. - For chat flows we recommend maintaining a small KV cache for context (we provide a sample cache wrapper in SDK).

3) Tool-calling / function execution model - We support structured function calls in the JSON response. Function signatures are verified server-side; Redwood issues a webhook to your product-lookup service when a call is required. Recommended pattern: return a function call token in the initial response, then exchange a signed call request. - Security: calls are HMAC-signed. We will include sample verification code for your microservice (Node + Java).

4) Observability & instrumentation - We'll ship a tracing hook and docs for correlating request_id across Redwood and LedgerCorp logs. We'll also provision a per-route cost dashboard so you can monitor projected spend in near real-time.

5) Test harness + evals - I'll attach a small test harness: a docker-compose with a stub product-lookup service + sample prompt sets. You can run locally and exercise the streaming flows.

Quick sample curl (embeddings):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-2","input":"How do I reset my password?"}'

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (includes sample SDK snippets and streaming notes)

I'll be present at the kickoff and will own the SDK integration work. Happy to jump on a separate call with your infra team if Rajiv prefers.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
